title: Dustless Popcorn Ceiling Removal | Gainesville & Ocala
description: Dustless popcorn ceiling removal with HEPA vacuum extraction and zip-wall containment for occupied homes in Gainesville, Ocala, and nearby Florida towns.
h1: Dustless Popcorn Ceiling Removal for Occupied Homes
heroIntro: A shrouded scraping and sanding setup connected to a HEPA vacuum captures texture and skim-coat dust at the source, so you can stay in your home while ceilings come down.
card: HEPA-extracted, contained popcorn removal that keeps dust out of ductwork, furniture, and nearby rooms.

secondary: popcorn ceiling removal while living in home
questions: Is dustless popcorn removal really dust free?
Can I stay home during popcorn ceiling removal?
Does dustless removal cost more than standard scraping?

body: Traditional texture removal relies on soaking and scraping, then sanding the new skim coat with open sanders. The debris lands on everything, and the finest particles from sanding drift into the next room and into the return side of your HVAC system, where they can circulate for weeks. Dustless popcorn ceiling removal changes where that material goes.

Scraping and sanding tools are fitted with shrouded heads connected to a HEPA-filtered vacuum, so most debris is pulled away the moment it leaves the ceiling. Zip-wall barriers seal the work area, and negative air keeps whatever is left inside it. The result is not a sterile operating room, but it is a large step up from open scraping in a lived-in house.

We describe the method plainly because the word dustless gets used loosely. Ask any contractor what tool the vacuum attaches to, whether sanding is captured as well as scraping, and how vents are sealed. Those answers tell you whether the setup is real. Dustless removal sits with our other specialty services and is quoted the same way: in writing, line by line.

sections.h2: Who should choose the dustless method
body: Standard removal works fine in an empty house or a room that can be cleared entirely. The dustless approach is worth it when that is not realistic:
bullets: Occupied homes where you need the kitchen, bedrooms, or home office to stay usable
Households with allergies, asthma, young children, or pets
Rooms full of furniture, built-ins, or electronics that cannot be moved out
Homes with open floor plans where a single plastic wall will not isolate the work
Condos and townhomes where shared ventilation or neighbors are a concern

sections.h2: Asbestos testing comes before any method
body: Dust control does not make hazardous material safe. Some ceiling texture installed before the mid-1980s contained asbestos, so older ceilings should be sampled and lab-tested before they are disturbed. If the test comes back positive, the work belongs to a licensed abatement contractor. Our article on testing popcorn ceilings for asbestos explains the steps.

Once a ceiling has been cleared, the dustless setup is about comfort and cleanliness, not hazard control. That distinction matters, and we would rather you hear it from us than assume a vacuum system makes any texture safe to remove.

sections.h2: Containment details that make the difference
body: The equipment only works if the setup is done carefully. Before any scraping starts, crews walk the room and the path to the exit and plan where barriers go. Typical details include:
bullets: Floor-to-ceiling zip walls with zippered entries at each doorway
Supply and return vents sealed so the HVAC system does not pull debris through the house
HEPA vacuum extraction at the scraper and the sanding head, not just a shop vac in the corner
Floors covered with taped-down protection and a clean walk-off zone at the entry
Daily cleanup so the contained area is tidy overnight while you are living in the home

sections.h2: How a dustless removal day runs
body: Crews set up containment first: zip walls at doorways, plastic over floors and anything staying in the room, and sealed vents and fixtures. Once the area is isolated, the texture is lightly misted and removed with the vacuum-shrouded scraper. Because the vacuum carries the debris away, there is far less wet sludge on the floor to track through the house.

After removal, joints and fasteners are repaired and the ceiling is skim coated. The sanding stage is where the finest dust is generated, and it is also captured at the sanding head. The ceiling is then primed and painted with a flat ceiling finish, or given a light knockdown texture if you prefer. Containment comes down only after a final vacuum and wipe-down.
For the full rundown of finish choices, ceiling repaints, and stained ceilings, see our main ceiling painting and popcorn removal service page.

sections.h2: Cost, timing, and what to expect afterward
body: The containment and extraction equipment adds setup time, so dustless removal costs somewhat more than open scraping. For many households that difference is smaller than the cost of deep-cleaning a whole house, replacing air filters repeatedly, or having ducts cleaned afterward. Your written estimate lists the ceilings included, the containment plan, the finish, and the products.

Work proceeds room by room so the rest of the house stays livable. If you are also refreshing walls, our interior painting crews can follow behind on the same project. Water-damaged or sagging drywall found once the texture is off is handled through our drywall repair service and priced before it is fixed.

faqs.q: Is dustless popcorn removal completely dust free?
faqs.a: No method is perfectly dust free, but capturing debris at the tool, isolating the room with zip walls, and running negative air keeps the vast majority of it out of your living space and HVAC system.

faqs.q: Can I stay home during the work?
faqs.a: Yes. That is the main reason people choose this method. Crews work one area at a time behind containment, so the rest of the house stays in use.

faqs.q: Does the dustless method work on asbestos texture?
faqs.a: No. Dust control is not abatement. Older texture should be lab-tested first, and positive results must be handled by a licensed abatement contractor.
